'''Peerio''' was a [[cross-platform]] [[End-to-end encryption|end-to-end encrypted]] application that provided secure messaging, file sharing, and cloud file storage. Peerio was available as an application for [[iOS]], [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[macOS]], [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]], and [[Linux]]. Peerio (Legacy) was originally released on 14 January 2015,<ref name=pcworld>{{cite web|last1=Paul|first1=Ian|title=Peerio hands-on: This secure messaging suite packs dead simple end-to-end encryption|url=http://www.pcworld.com/article/2871254/peerio-hands-on-this-secure-messaging-suite-packs-dead-simple-end-to-end-encryption.html|website=PC World|accessdate=19 May 2015|date=15 January 2015}}</ref><ref name=Wired>{{cite magazine|last1=Greenberg|first1=Andy|title=The Free Encryption App That Wants to Replace Gmail, Dropbox, and HipChat|url=https://www.wired.com/2015/01/peerio-free-encryption-app/|magazine=Wired|accessdate=19 May 2015|date=14 January 2015}}</ref> and was replaced by Peerio 2 on 15 June 2017.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://medium.com/@saumyaarora/the-new-peerio-a-brand-new-architecture-a-brand-new-experience-5f54c40f185d|title=The NEW Peerio: A Brand New Architecture. A Brand New Experience.|last=Arora|first=Saumya|date=2017-06-15|website=Medium|access-date=2018-01-30}}</ref> The app is discontinued.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://alternativeto.net/software/peerio/|title=Peerio Alternatives and Similar Apps}}</ref>

Messages and user files stored on the Peerio cloud were protected by end-to-end encryption, meaning the data was encrypted in a way that could not be read by third parties, such as Peerio itself or its service providers. Security was provided by a single permanent key-password, which in Peerio was called an "Account Key".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://te-st.ru/2017/09/13/peerio-2-the-new-version-of-the-protected-instant-messenger/|title=PEERIO-2 - THE NEW VERSION OF THE SECURE MESSENGER|last1=Lomov|first1=Vladimir|date=19 September 2017|website=te-st.ru|publisher=te-st|accessdate=13 September 2017}}</ref>

The company, Peerio Technologies Inc., was founded in 2014 by Vincent Drouin. The intent behind Peerio was to provide a security program that is easier to use than the [[Pretty Good Privacy|PGP]] standard.<ref name="Gigaom">{{cite web|url=https://gigaom.com/2015/01/14/peerio-is-a-chat-and-storage-service-with-big-security-claims/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150114172410/https://gigaom.com/2015/01/14/peerio-is-a-chat-and-storage-service-with-big-security-claims/|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 14, 2015|title=Peerio is a chat and storage service with big security claims|last1=Meyer|first1=David|date=14 January 2015|website=Gigaom|accessdate=19 May 2015}}</ref>

Peerio was acquired by [[WorkJam (software company)|WorkJam]], a digital workplace solutions provider, on January 13, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=WorkJam acquires secure chat platform Peerio |url=https://betakit.com/workjam-acquires-secure-chat-platform-peerio/ |website=BetaKit |accessdate=2019-11-19 |language=en-CA |date=14 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Releases |first1=Business Wire News |title=WorkJam Announces Acquisition of Peerio Technologies {{!}} Financial Post |url=https://business.financialpost.com/pmn/press-releases-pmn/business-wire-news-releases-pmn/workjam-announces-acquisition-of-peerio-technologies |accessdate=2019-11-19 |date=2019-01-13 |language=en-CA}}</ref>

==Features==
Peerio allowed users to share encrypted messages and files in direct messages or groups that Peerio called "rooms".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.peerio.com/index.html|title=Peerio|website=www.peerio.com|access-date=2018-01-31}}</ref>

Peerio "rooms" were offered as a team-oriented group chat, allowing administrative functionality to add and remove other users from the group chat.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.peerio.com/creating-a-secure-workspace-peerio-rooms.html|title=Peerio|website=www.peerio.com|access-date=2018-01-31}}</ref>

Peerio allows users to store encrypted files online, offering limited cloud storage for free with optional paid upgrades.<ref name=":0" />

Peerio messages and files [[Persistent data structure|persist]] between logins and hardware, differing from [[Ephemeral data structure|ephemeral]] encrypted messaging apps which do not retain message or file history between logins or different devices.

Peerio supported application based [[multi-factor authentication]].<ref name=":0" />

Peerio allowed users to share animated GIFs.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.peerio.com/3-2-1-saying-goodbye-to-peerio-legacy.html|title=Peerio|website=www.peerio.com|access-date=2018-01-31}}</ref>

==Security==

=== End-to-End Encryption ===

Peerio utilized end-to-end encryption and it was applied by default to all message and file data. End-to-end encryption is intended to encrypt data in a way that only the sender and intended recipients are able to decrypt, and thus read, the data.

Taken from Peerio's privacy policy:

"Peerio utilizes the [[NaCl (software)|NaCl]] (pronounced "salt") cryptographic framework, which itself uses the following cryptographic primitives:
*  ''[[X25519]]'' for public key agreement over elliptic curves.
* ''[[ed25519]]'' for public key signatures.
*  ''XSalsa20'' for encryption and confidentiality.
*  ''[[Poly1305]]'' for ensuring the integrity of encrypted data.
Additionally, Peerio uses ''[[scrypt]]'' for memory-hard key derivation and ''[[BLAKE2s]]'' is used for various hashing operations.

For in-transit encryption, Peerio Services used [[Transport Layer Security]] (TLS) with best-practice cipher suite configuration, including support for [[Perfect Forward Secrecy|perfect forward secrecy]] (PFS). You can view a detailed and up-to-date independent review of Peerio's TLS configuration on SSL Labs."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html?d=icebear.peerio.com|title=SSL Server Test: icebear.peerio.com (Powered by Qualys SSL Labs)|website=www.ssllabs.com|access-date=2018-01-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.peerio.com/privacy.html|title=Peerio|website=www.peerio.com|access-date=2018-01-30}}</ref>

=== Code Audits ===

Prior to Peerio's initial release, the software was [[Software audit review|audited]] by the German security firm [[Cure53]], which found only non-security related bugs, all of which were fixed prior to the applications release.<ref name="Wired" />

According to Peerio's website, the application was also audited in March 2017 by Cure53.<ref name=":1" />

=== Open Source ===

Peerio was partly [[Open-source software|open source]] and published code publicly on [[GitHub]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://github.com/PeerioTechnologies|title=Peerio Technologies|website=GitHub|language=en|access-date=2018-01-31}}</ref>

=== Bug Bounty ===

Peerio offered a [[Bug bounty program|bug bounty]], offering cash rewards for anyone who reports security vulnerabilities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.peerio.com/bug.html|title=Peerio|website=www.peerio.com|access-date=2018-01-31}}</ref>

==Peerio (Legacy)==
The first iteration of Peerio, '''Peerio (Legacy)''', was developed by [[Nadim Kobeissi]] and Florencia Herra-Vega and was released on 14 January 2015<ref name="pcworld" /><ref name="Wired" /> and was closed on 8 January 2018.<ref name=":2" />

Peerio (Legacy) was a free application, available for [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[iOS]], [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]], [[macOS]], [[Linux]], and as a [[Google Chrome extension]].<ref name="SocialTimes">{{cite web|url=http://www.adweek.com/socialtimes/peerio-simple-encryption-for-the-masses/613227|title=Peerio: Simple Encryption for the Masses|last1=Morrison|first1=Kimberlee|date=22 January 2015|website=SocialTimes|accessdate=19 May 2015}}</ref><ref name="Peerio">{{cite web|url=http://blog.peerio.com/post/141088039469/android-and-ios-apps-are-here|title=Android and iOS apps are here!|last1=Peerio|date=15 March 2016|website=Peerio|accessdate=16 March 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160321065435/http://blog.peerio.com/post/141088039469/android-and-ios-apps-are-here|archivedate=21 March 2016}}</ref>  It offered end-to-end encryption, which is enabled by default.  The encryption used the miniLock open-source security standard, which was also developed by Kobeissi.<ref name="zdnet">{{cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/nsa-busting-encryption-app-peerio-puts-privacy-first/|title=Meet the free encryption app that promises to put your privacy first|last1=Whittaker|first1=Zack|date=2 March 2015|website=ZDNnet.com|access-date=19 May 2015}}</ref>

On 15 June 2017, Peerio 2 was launched as the successor to Peerio (Legacy). According to the company's blog, Peerio 2 is purported to be a "radical overhaul" of the original application's core technology.<ref name=":3" /> Claimed benefits in comparison to Peerio (Legacy) include increased speed, support for larger file transfers (up to 7000GB), and a re-designed user interface. Peerio also stated an added focus towards businesses looking for encrypted team collaboration software.<ref name=":1" />
